description: ODC (EDIT coverage for the UI): touch a SCREEN and a BLOCK that this job did not create. The base is job:screen-list (which inherits job:screen-form and job:data-full-model), so by the time the first op runs, the screen WfCovTasks already exists with its aggregate, the layout block instance, the List with the ListItem and the two expressions inside it, and the New button in the Actions placeholder. There is not a single op here that creates a screen, block or instance: everything that follows is maintenance on top of what the other job left written. The five changes are: (1) properties of the inherited screen itself - Title, Description and its own StyleSheet; (2) two arguments of the inherited block INSTANCE, which is the point where a screen configures the layout it received; (3) properties of the inherited BLOCK LayoutTopMenu, which was born from no job - it came with the module and has six consumers; (4) properties of inherited WIDGETS - the List's Style and AnimateItems, the text inside the button; (5) two widgets added INSIDE the container that already existed (the 'content' placeholder of the ListItem, which already had two expressions) plus two reorderings, one of the new widget and one of an INHERITED widget. Outside the job that created them there are no aliases: the screen is cited as 'IMobileScreen:WfCovTasks', the block as 'IMobileBlock:LayoutTopMenu', and a child by the path from there; the same form holds inside the arguments. Each change has its get BEFORE and its get AFTER, and at the end the things this job did NOT touch are read - the neighbouring screen WfCovTaskDetail and the ExtendedClass argument of the OTHER instance of the same block - to see what is per instance and what is shared. NOTE ON THE DATA CONTRACT: since this run it also watches top-level named elements, and a screen (IMobileScreen) and a block (IMobileBlock) are two of them. The screen's Title and Description and the block's Description are remembered and checked at the end: if the write had not taken effect, the job would fail with 'Data property mismatch' even with a clean Verify. The StyleSheet, on the other hand, is in the list of properties that are read another way and is NOT watched - therefore, and only therefore, the screen's StyleSheet and the block's each get an explicit get right after: it is the only proof that this text got in.

ops.name: WfCovTasks
ops._why: (0) starting point: the screen ALREADY exists before the first op of this job. It comes from the base job:screen-list, not from a create here. It is the difference between a birth job and a maintenance job: if the screen were created in this file, none of the five changes below would prove any editing

(1) BEFORE, the screen: Title null, Description null, StyleSheet empty - a screen freshly created by the minimal recipe carries none of this. Note also Widgets 20 and ScreenAggregates 1, to compare with the get (10b): the property changes neither add nor remove widgets

(2) BEFORE, the whole inherited tree: the aggregate GetTasks with its source and its sort, the IMobileBlockInstanceWidget with THREE IArgument and SIX placeholders (Header, Breadcrumbs, Title, Actions, MainContent, Footer), the List with the ListItem and, inside the item's 'content' placeholder, the two expressions in this order: Title and then DueOn. This is the snapshot the dump (18) is compared with

(3) BEFORE, the inherited block. This one did not even come from a job: it was born with the module (CreatedByTool ODCStudio) and the Description that is read is the template's. Referrers 6, and that is what makes change (3) a shared change and not a local one

(4) BEFORE, who holds it, by name - and the count misleads anyone who does not open it: count 6, real 6, but byType says FIVE IMobileBlockInstanceWidget and ONE IMobileTheme. The five instances are the screens InvalidPermissions, UserProfile, ChangePassword, this job's WfCovTasks and the WfCovTaskDetail of job:screen-form; the sixth consumer is not an instance at all, it is the InsuranceApp theme itself, which designates this block as the default layout. It serves to show in the usages (13) that editing the block's properties neither creates nor breaks any consumer - author text and CSS are not references

(5) BEFORE, the block instance INSIDE the screen: SourceBlock points to the key of LayoutTopMenu, Arguments 3, PlaceholdersContent 6. The instance has no name - that is why the path uses '#IMobileBlockInstanceWidget', the n-th child of that type, and not a name

(6) BEFORE, the argument that will change: Value null. An IArgument has no name of its own - it is resolved by the NAME OF THE PARAMETER of the producer block (ExtendedClass is one of the three IInputParameter of LayoutTopMenu), and the property that is written is called Value

(7) BEFORE, the second argument: also Value null, that is, the inherited instance accepted the block's default. I chose two arguments that NOBODY had written, so that change (2) is really the configuration of an inherited instance and not the correction of a value this job had set

(8) BEFORE, an inherited widget: Style "list list-group" and AnimateItems True, both written by the platform when the List was born, and Source GetTasks.List, which was indeed written by the base job. Compare with the get (14b)

(9) BEFORE, the container that already existed: the 'content' placeholder of the ListItem, with TWO inherited expressions, in this order - GetTasks.List.Current.WfCovTask.Title and then .DueOn. And it is inside this container, and only inside it, that change (5) adds and reorders

(10a) CHANGE 1 - properties of the inherited screen. Title is the PAGE title (what the browser shows in the tab), not the text in the header: that one is the expression "Tasks" that the base job put inside the Title placeholder of the block instance, and it is still there, intact, in the dump (18). They are two things with the same name and different owners. Title is an expression property of a top-level named element, so it is WATCHED by the data contract: if the write had not taken effect, the job would fail at the end

ops.value: Lista de tarefas abertas. Description escrita por screen-block-edit.json, DEPOIS de a tela existir.
ops._why: the Description of the screen was empty; it is also watched. Note the contrast with the Description of the BLOCK in change 3: that one was not empty, it had the template's text, and therefore there it is a replacement and here it is a fill

the screen's OWN StyleSheet - the CSS that only this page loads. Unlike the StyleSheet of a THEME, which has three halves in the model (generated, the author's, and the derived one that is read), a screen's is plain text: what is written is what is read. But the data contract treats the two alike and watches NEITHER, because the list of asymmetric properties is by property NAME; that is why the get (10b) exists. The classes written here are the same ones that change 2 and change 5 start to use

(10b) AFTER: compare with the get (1). Title, Description and StyleSheet CHANGED; Name, Public False, Widgets 20 and ScreenAggregates 1 STAYED - none of these writes touched the tree. This get is the ONLY proof of the StyleSheet (not watched); Title and Description also have, besides it, the contract check at the end of the job

(11a) CHANGE 2 - an argument of the INHERITED block instance. This is how a screen configures the layout it received, without touching the block: the class that goes in here is the same one the screen's StyleSheet defines, and this argument is where the two halves meet. The path cites the parameter by name INSIDE the instance, which is the form that holds outside the job that created the instance

the second argument, now boolean - but written as an OutSystems EXPRESSION ("True", text), and not as JSON true, because what an IArgument stores in Value is always an expression. In a long list the fixed header is the right choice, and this screen is a list

(11b) AFTER: Value with the class, and the Parameter still pointing to the SAME key of the block's IInputParameter - the value changed, not the link. An IArgument is deliberately not watched by the data contract: the platform RECREATES the arguments when the block's contract changes, and remembering those keys would give a false positive. Here the proof is this get
AFTER, the other argument: Value True

ops.value: Layout de topo do InsuranceApp. Description reescrita por screen-block-edit.json por cima do texto que veio no template do modulo.
ops._why: (12a) CHANGE 3 - properties of the inherited BLOCK. This is the job's strongest inheritance case: LayoutTopMenu came neither from the base nor from any job, it came with the module, and has six consumers that this job did not choose. The Description was NOT empty - it said 'Adds a layout with the menu on the header...' -, so here there is a real replacement of author text. IMobileBlock is a top-level named element: this write is watched

the block's own StyleSheet, scoped to the class that the screen injects through the ExtendedClass argument: the CSS lives in the block, but it only paints the screens that ask for the class. It is the same mechanism as the screen's StyleSheet and the same gap - it is not watched, only the get (12b) proves it

(12b) AFTER: compare with the get (3). Description and StyleSheet CHANGED; Name, InputParameters 3, Widgets 30, ScreenActions 4 and Referrers 6 STAYED - editing the text and the CSS of a block does not touch its contract or its consumers
(13) AFTER: exactly the list of the usages (4), with the same keys. Description and StyleSheet are text, not references - the six consumers are still the same six, five instances and the theme

(14a) CHANGE 4 - properties of inherited WIDGETS. The Style of the List had "list list-group", written by the platform at the birth of the widget; here the module's class is added on top. A widget is NOT a top-level named element: it does not enter the data contract, because the platform recreates widgets when a contract changes. What proves a write like this is the get (14b)

a truly boolean property, and not an expression property: it takes JSON false, without quotes - the opposite of the argument's Value in change 2. The entry animation of the items gets in the way in a list that reloads on every filter

the caption of the inherited button. In ODC the text of a button is not a property of it: it is an ITextWidget inside its IContent, so the path goes down one more level. That is also why no future rename follows this caption - it is text, not a binding

(14b) AFTER: compare with the get (8). Style and AnimateItems CHANGED; Source GetTasks.List, Widgets 1 and the key of the ListItem STAYED - changing the appearance of an inherited widget does not touch its data or its children
AFTER, the button: the Style "btn btn-primary" that nobody touched is still there, and the OnClick still points to WfCovTaskDetail. Only the caption changed

ops.name: WfTaskStatus
ops._why: (15a) CHANGE 5 - add INSIDE a container that already existed. The parent is not a $alias: aliases are local to the job that declares them, and the one who declared this ListItem was the base job. The name carries the Wf prefix because it is a NEW element; naming an expression is optional, but here it pays off so that the move ops (15c/15d) return a readable order instead of four identical <IExpression>
reads the current record by the name of the INHERITED aggregate (GetTasks): the new expression enters the scope the screen already had, with no need to declare anything
the class that the StyleSheet of the screen (change 1) defined. The three changes close the circuit: CSS in the screen, layout class in the argument of the instance, item class in the new widget

ops.name: WfTaskLate
ops._why: (15b) the second new widget, in the same container. Both enter at the END of the sequence, which is where the platform puts whatever is born - the order that is wanted comes next, via move, and not from the order of the creates
only functions from the Studio catalog: If, CurrDate and the operators not/and/<. Names from other languages (IIf, Now, DateDiff) do not exist and the runner catches them before the Verify

(15c) REORDER, first the new widget. '#IExpression[1]' is the FIRST child of that type (the index is 1-based, not 0) and at this point it is still the INHERITED title expression, because the two new ones entered at the end. Resulting order, in the result of the op itself: <IExpression>, WfTaskStatus, <IExpression>, WfTaskLate

(15d) and now an INHERITED widget, which is the proof that matters: after the previous move the order is [Title, WfTaskStatus, DueOn, WfTaskLate], so index 3 is the DueOn expression, created by the OTHER job. Sending it to the end gives [Title, WfTaskStatus, WfTaskLate, DueOn]. The move REORDERS within the same parent - it does not reparent: 'before'/'after' of an object of another parent is refused

(15e) AFTER, the container: compare with the dump (9). There were two expressions in the order [Title, DueOn]; there are four in the order [Title, WfTaskStatus, WfTaskLate, DueOn]. The proof of the order is in the text of each expression, not in the name - the two inherited ones are still unnamed, as they were born

(16) WHAT STAYED: the neighbouring screen, from the same base (job:screen-form), intact - Title null, Description null, StyleSheet empty, the same values that WfCovTasks had in the get (1). It is the counter-proof that the writes of change 1 hit THAT screen and not a reconstruction of the interface

(17) WHAT STAYED, and the lesson on what is shared: this is another of the five instances of the SAME block that change 3 edited. Value is still null - an argument is per instance. The Description and the StyleSheet of the block, on the other hand, this screen received without knowing, because they belong to the block and not to the instance. Two similar changes, opposite reach

(18) The final tree, to put next to the dump (2): the same children, in the same order, with the aggregate GetTasks and the six placeholders where they were; the "Tasks" expression of the Title placeholder is still the base job's (the PAGE's Title, which this job wrote, does not appear here because it is a property of the screen, not a widget); and the only structural difference is the two new expressions inside the 'content' of the ListItem. Everything else that changed was a property, and a property is not seen in the tree - it is seen in the gets
